questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As an English student, the language spoken in the country of destination was the most crucial. My choice of university in the UK depended heavily on safety (I wanted to go somewhere were I could easily and safely get from A to B at all hours). The second other important factor for me was the reputation and high academic standard of the university. Finally, I chose the UK, because the expenses of travelling to and living are lower than what is the case for Canada, Australia and the US.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: St Andrews is a lovely study town and the university offers an incredibly unique social life and inspiring teaching. It is also beautiful and safe.  However, as a master's student who has never had any issues keeping up with the work load at Copenhagen University and who has continually received high marks, I was pushed to my absolute limit as a postgraduate at St Andrews School of English. At times, I experienced stress and anxiety symptoms due to the high pressure to meet all my deadlines. This also meant, I did not have as much time to socialise and enjoy the culture as many other exchange students. However, I also grew as an academic and achieved skills I had not expected to achieve in such a short time. Hence, I would recommend the postgraduate programme at St Andrews School of English to those of my fellow students who wishes to go on exchange for academic opportunities mostly.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a helpful orientation app.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Information was apt and accessible, but I wish the global office or the school of English would have put us into some groups or planned some social activities for each class, so you have someone to go to these events with outside your dorm. It was very overwhelming trying to find a group of like-minded students the first couple of days through a WhatsApp group with hundreds of members.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You received one offer and as it took my host institution some time to process my application not a lot of options were left. But housing is guaranteed,  and the accommodation office were very helpful in finding a place that matched my needs.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Great cooking facilities and meal plans available.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: If you want as many opportunities to socialise as possible choose a hall with limited cooking facilties which is fully catered. You meet a lot of people in the dinning hall. The less expensive and calm option, where you have your own space would be sharing a kitchen with four others. My kitchen was always chill and pretty clean and the people I shared it with were super friendly.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The only downside to accommodation in St Andrews is the price level. It is very pricy, but it is nice, clean and safe.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Before my stay, it was quite demanding and slow. It all happened via email and it was well into June before I received a final confirmation that I was actually going which was quite stressing because it left me little time to sublet my flat and terminate my job. When I got there, it was very easy and efficient.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A whole array of help was available and a lot of effort was put into informing us and even encouraging us to reach out for help whenever we needed it during orientation week.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Quite succesfull. I had listed to courses back in May that I was interested in taking, but three days before departing I was asked to send a 1000 word essay so that they could decide if I was qualified. In the end, I got two other classes that I had also listed as relevant. I would just have appreciated an earlier notice for that other essay than three days before departure.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient but make sure to follow up regularly via email so the prioritise your application.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The themes and modules were incredibly inspiring and high level. The study facilities and classrooms were also top tier. However, I only received four hours of teaching a week, so I spent a lot of time doing independent studying, trying to keep up with assignment deadlines. That did take its toll on me mentally and I would have loved some more time in class with other students and a teacher.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: SCQF level 11, 30 ects in total.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar. Dialogue based with lots of time for class discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: EN5504 Reading the Modern & EN5503 Contextualising the Modern at University of St Andrews

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend these two courses (EN5504 Reading the Modern & EN5503 Contextualising the Modern) to any students who are passionate about literature and ready for an academic challenge. If you are looking to apply for a PhD in English Literature in the future, this is definitely the course for you.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I had almost no transportion costs because everything is within walking distance in St Andrews but travelling around Scotland can be quite expensive. Food is a little less expensive than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many clubs and opportunities to socialise if you can find the time outside your studies.  The breakaway society is a great way to see more of Scotland if you are on a budget. Not a lot of socialising happened in with my classmates  since we only saw each other four hours a week, so at St Andrews, it is important to be outgoing and join some of the university clubs' events and pub socials.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Breakaway, yoga and book society.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking and hang out with people from your dorm and try to reach out to some of the other students from Copenhagen Uni through the Facebook group shared by the global office.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. St Andrews is super international - 30% are American.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Again, joining the pub socials for a club that catches your interest. Or ask your classmates out for a pint.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: British people can be a little bit more formal, especially in class, so be conscious of how direct you are in your communication. But I would not worry about that to much. Scottish people are so kind, chatty and funny!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Scottish humour and helpfulness as well as their folk dance and pub culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) If you are a postgraduate, make sure you are up for an academic challenge 2) If you want an easy way to socialise, pay for that expensive catered meal plan (those who did said it was worth it) 3) find the other few Danes in St Andrews because it is nice to have those to share your ups and downs with.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get started on your assignments in due time and try to visit your teachers during their office hours - they are among the best scholars in the world, so make use of it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: St Andrews and Scotland is marvellously pretty and charming. It is like a fairytale town and the study spaces are straight out of Hogwarts.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Keeping up with the deadlines and spending so much time in my own company because class time was so sparse.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
